comments.value:
Do you know the number of draw calls those avatars use? It's definitely possible to tank performance with raw draw call count, and a mirror would make that much worse.

Could you elaborate more on the VRAM aspect? Is near-full VRAM required for the issue? If so, it might be possible that the graphics card drivers are swapping textures between dedicated and shared ram, and this is appearing as CPU time.

@{62e1338f5d95dd469bfc8f94|full_name}: If you use a profile locally, you know that draw calls roughly account for pen overhead. Before EAC, you can directly get the CPU usage occupied by draw calls.

In addition, it is not the CPU overhead caused by the high VRAM itself. The mechanism is completely different and has been tested.

High VRAM is only maintained in this state. Avatars that do not meet the conditions will immediately drop back to normal CPU usage and frame time.

By my own count, about 10% of CPU overhead comes from draw calls. Opening the mirror is equivalent to adding an extra camera. The more the avatar is sampled by the camera, the more the overhead will increase

Camera CPU frame time bursts only sampled for avatars with large borders and hundreds of PhysBone components

I just turned on a mirror and let the camera on the avatar shine on one of the problematic avatars. The judgment is not enough to increase the draw call significantly, but the fact is different from the imagination, just like the game logic cost has doubled.

details:
Found that in some cases, no one in the FOV can have an unusually high CPU overhead

According to the CPU frame time detected by fpsVR, it should be 7~8ms under normal circumstances, but after triggering this problem, it will go directly to 22~30ms, resulting in the frame rate being limited to about 33fps.

1. Requires an avatar with enough PhysBone components

2. The three bounds values of the avatar are all very large

3. Things related to udon and the mirror of this world

Or use the avatar with a camera or the avatar of a friend with a camera after mirroring is turned on in the world. At this time, the CPU overhead is extremely high

Originally, all the avatars in the FOV are about 10ms, 12ms after turning on the camera, and directly become 24~25ms after adding other cameras.

If VRAM is close to full, it will remain under high load. If you open the mirror and look at other avatar, the frame time of the CPU will reach a new high of 30ms or even 35ms.

I've found this to happen a lot in vrchat, and it's hard to realize it's a problem. Because it can be solved when a specific avatar or avatar is left or replaced, but the VRAM high load state will persist, even re-entering the world or changing avatar cannot solve it.

But if the problem is not triggered, even if the VRAM is close to full, even if you leave the border of the avatar, the CPU frame time will immediately drop back to 7~8ms.

I want to confirm if this is a bug in game logic or a feature?

Under normal circumstances in Unity3D, turning on mirroring should not cause the game logic load to explode. Only draw calls are included in the profile, and the normal game draw call load is very low, even if the draw call of the skin mesh is very expensive.
title: CPU overhead unusual
